text: PVDF-TrFE-CFE has been well-characterized using different methods in the literature.13,15,31 An IR camera was selected to characterize the EC performance due to its efficiency and effectiveness, and it had shown reliable results in the literature successfully (Table 2). The thickness of the annealed films was measured using focused ion beam SEM. Electrocaloric performance is shown in using an IR camera. When interpreting this data, it is important to note that the electrocaloric ∆T is electric-field dependent, where higher electric fields lead to larger ∆T . Figure 5a-c demonstrates the temperature change after applying an electric ECE field which was successfully captured by the IR camera. There is no detectable ∆T when the ECE films are not annealed and the applied electric field less is than 100 MV/m (Figure 5d, black symbols). For electric fields less than 100 MV/m, there is no significant difference in ∆T ECE between ES A60 film and ES A120 films after running statistical analysis. Overall, it’s confirmed that the ∆T of ES A120 film (Figure 5d, blue symbols) is larger than ES A60 film (Figure 5d, ECE 14 DE-EE0009099 red symbols) at 100 MV/m. An independent t-test from Rstudio (version 2024.09.1+394) indicates there is a statistical significance between ES A120 and ES A60 at 100 MV/m at a p value < 0.05. This result may be attributed to the ES A120 film’s larger dielectric constant, larger degree of crystallinity, and possible more ordered crystalline phase, all of which can lead to an increase in the EC temperature change. There is another additional effect that may further enhance the EC effect of ES A120 film, which is that a high annealing temperature of the terpolymer can lead to larger thermal stress. The increase in stress levels can contribute to the enhancement of the EC effect.12,32 The highest measured EC ∆T is 4.1˚C and the average ∆T is 3.6˚C  0.5 ˚C for ES ECE A120 film, which was observed at room temperature at 100 MV/m. Figure 5e presents the data in a slightly different way by normalizing the ∆T by the applied electric field, where it is shown ECE that a slightly larger EC lift of ∆T /E is obtained at a low field from ES A60 film, whereas the ECE ∆T /E of ES A120 film is 0.084 ˚Cm/MV at 100 MV/m and 22˚C. However, it is noted that ECE there are many other factors, including mechanical stresses, ambient temperature, crystallite dimension, and dipole polarity, which could also vary the electrocaloric performance of the PVDF- TrFE-CFE films. This manuscript only concludes the study of PVDF-TrFE-CFE film between thermal energy, dielectric energy, the estimated crystallite size, thin film surface analysis and electrocaloric performance. Other literature has found the electrocaloric effect of relaxor ferroelectric polymer can be dominated by the crystalline size at the low to modest electric field (between 20 MV/m and 80 MV/m).
